Attributed ASTIS-authored scoped mathematical completion, not a verbatim numbered source theorem.
E is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert Borel space with canonical volume; rank zero is an explicit extension of the source Euclidean convention. V:E→ℝ is C²; 0<α≤β; α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖² for every x,v; η>0 and βη≤1. μ=volume.tilted(−V), J=Law(X,X+√ηZ) for independent X∼μ and Z∼N(0,I), and ν=J.snd. Finite dimensionality of E does not imply finite dimensionality of L²(ν). Let Λ be the law of (Y,2X−Y) under J, F(x,y)=(x,2x−y), and P the L²(J) conditional-expectation orthogonal projection onto the second-coordinate sigma algebra. The laws μ,J,ν are probabilities. There exist a Markov kernel S with, for every y, S(y)=volume.tilted(x↦−V((y+x)/2)−‖y−x‖²/(8η)), Λ disintegrated by S and both marginals equal to ν; an involutive selfadjoint linear isometry U with Ug=g∘F J-a.e.; an isometric pullback M with Mu=u∘snd J-a.e.; and a selfadjoint T on L²(ν) such that for every u, PMu=Mu, MTu=PUPMu, ‖Tu‖≤‖u‖, Tu(y)=∫u(x)S(y,dx) ν-a.e. and ∫Tu dν=∫u dν. There is a constant class q=1 ν-a.e. with Tq=q and ⟨q,u⟩=∫u dν for all u. Its exact closed orthogonal kernel H₀ is all of L²₀(ν). The full defect D=I−T² is positive, Dq=0 and ⟨Du,u⟩=‖u‖²−‖Tu‖² for all u. The actual restriction T₀:H₀→H₀ agrees with T on every u∈H₀, is selfadjoint and contractive. D₀=I_H₀−T₀² is positive, agrees with D as an ambient L² class on H₀, and satisfies ⟨D₀u,u⟩=‖u‖²−‖T₀u‖² for all u∈H₀.

    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0} {η : ℝ}
    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)

      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ)*‖v‖^2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ)*η ≤ 1) :
    let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -V x)
    let J := (μ.prod (stdGaussian E)).map
      (fun p : E × E => (p.1,p.1+Real.sqrt η • p.2))
    let ν := J.snd
    let Λ := J.map (fun p : E × E => (p.2,(2 : ℝ) • p.1-p.2))
    let F := fun p : E × E => (p.1,(2 : ℝ) • p.1-p.2)
    let P : Lp ℝ 2 J →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J :=

        2 J).subtypeL ∘L condExpL2 ℝ ℝ measurable_snd.comap_le
    IsProbabilityMeasure μ ∧ IsProbabilityMeasure J ∧ IsProbabilityMeasure ν ∧
    ∃ S : Kernel E E, IsMarkovKernel S ∧

      Λ.IsCondKernel S ∧ Λ.fst = ν ∧ Λ.snd = ν ∧

        (∀ g : Lp ℝ 2 J, (U g : E × E → ℝ) =ᵐ[J] g ∘ F) ∧
        Function.Involutive U ∧ IsSelfAdjoint U.toContinuousLinearMap ∧
        ∃ M : Lp ℝ 2 ν →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J,
          (∀ u : Lp ℝ 2 ν, (M u : E × E → ℝ) =ᵐ[J] u ∘ Prod.snd) ∧

              M (T u) = (P * U.toContinuousLinearMap * P) (M u) ∧

decoder_context: The underlying space is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert Borel space with canonical volume, including zero dimension. The potential is C2 with positive alpha<=beta, both displayed global Hessian bounds, eta>0 and beta*eta<=1.

Measure.tilted is normalized exponential tilting. The displayed joint is the pushforward of the independent product of the tilted law and the standard Gaussian; the marginal is its second-coordinate law. Lp real exponent 2 denotes AE classes of measurable square-integrable real functions. Its dimension need not be finite.

The displayed conditional projection is the L2 conditional expectation onto the second-coordinate sigma algebra. Operator multiplication denotes composition; the typed identity acts on the displayed entire domain. The kernel of innerSL(q) is the full closed real subspace orthogonal to q. An inverse expressed by IsUnit belongs to the algebra of bounded continuous linear endomorphisms of exactly that domain.

The existential kernel is produced as a Markov kernel with the every-state displayed normalized density. Its conditional joint law and both marginals, the AE reflection/isometry, the actual pullback, the operator, constant and centered restriction are conclusions, not caller-supplied certificates.

IsPositive is positivity of a selfadjoint quadratic form on the displayed Hilbert domain. The full defect annihilates the constant, while the centered defect is its actual restriction. The squared defect is not a chosen positive square root.

    let P : Lp ℝ 2 J →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J :=
      (lpMeas ℝ ℝ (MeasurableSpace.comap Prod.snd (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace E))
        2 J).subtypeL ∘L condExpL2 ℝ ℝ measurable_snd.comap_le
    IsProbabilityMeasure μ ∧ IsProbabilityMeasure J ∧ IsProbabilityMeasure ν ∧
    ∃ S : Kernel E E, IsMarkovKernel S ∧
      (∀ y, S y = (volume : Measure E).tilted
        (fun x => -V ((1/2 : ℝ) • (y+x)) - ‖y-x‖^2/(8*η))) ∧
      Λ.IsCondKernel S ∧ Λ.fst = ν ∧ Λ.snd = ν ∧
      ∃ U : Lp ℝ 2 J →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J,
        (∀ g : Lp ℝ 2 J, (U g : E × E → ℝ) =ᵐ[J] g ∘ F) ∧
        Function.Involutive U ∧ IsSelfAdjoint U.toContinuousLinearMap ∧
        ∃ M : Lp ℝ 2 ν →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J,
          (∀ u : Lp ℝ 2 ν, (M u : E × E → ℝ) =ᵐ[J] u ∘ Prod.snd) ∧
          ∃ T : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν,
            IsSelfAdjoint T ∧
            (∀ u : Lp ℝ 2 ν,
              P (M u) = M u ∧
              M (T u) = (P * U.toContinuousLinearMap * P) (M u) ∧
              ‖T u‖ ≤ ‖u‖ ∧
              (T u : E → ℝ) =ᵐ[ν] (fun y => ∫ x, u x ∂S y) ∧
              (∫ y, T u y ∂ν) = ∫ y, u y ∂ν) ∧
            ∃ q : Lp ℝ 2 ν,
              (q : E → ℝ) =ᵐ[ν] (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) ∧ T q = q ∧
              (∀ u : Lp ℝ 2 ν, inner ℝ q u = ∫ y, u y ∂ν) ∧
              (∀ u : Lp ℝ 2 ν, u ∈ ((innerSL ℝ q).ker) ↔ (∫ y, u y ∂ν) = 0) ∧
              ((1 : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν)-T*T).IsPositive ∧ ((1 : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν)-T*T) q = 0 ∧
              (∀ u : Lp ℝ 2 ν,
                inner ℝ (((1 : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν)-T*T) u) u = ‖u‖^2-‖T u‖^2) ∧
              ∃ T0 : ((innerSL ℝ q).ker) →L[ℝ] ((innerSL ℝ q).ker),
                (∀ u : ((innerSL ℝ q).ker), (T0 u : Lp ℝ 2 ν) = T u) ∧
                IsSelfAdjoint T0 ∧ (∀ u : ((innerSL ℝ q).ker), ‖T0 u‖ ≤ ‖u‖) ∧
                ((1 : ((innerSL ℝ q).ker) →L[ℝ] ((innerSL ℝ q).ker))-T0*T0).IsPositive ∧
                (∀ u : ((innerSL ℝ q).ker), (((1 : ((innerSL ℝ q).ker) →L[ℝ] ((innerSL ℝ q).ker))-T0*T0) u : Lp ℝ 2 ν) = ((1 : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν)-T*T) u) ∧
                (∀ u : ((innerSL ℝ q).ker),

  classical
  dsimp only
  let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -V x)
  let J := (μ.prod (stdGaussian E)).map
    (fun p : E × E => (p.1,p.1+Real.sqrt η • p.2))
  let ν := J.snd
  let Λ := J.map (fun p : E × E => (p.2,(2 : ℝ) • p.1-p.2))
  let P : Lp ℝ 2 J →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J :=
    (lpMeas ℝ ℝ (MeasurableSpace.comap Prod.snd (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace E))
      2 J).subtypeL ∘L condExpL2 ℝ ℝ measurable_snd.comap_le
  have hBase := L2MacroscopicMean.actual_macroscopic_l2_mean hα hαβ hV hH hη hβη
  rcases hBase with ⟨hμ,hJ,hν,S,hS,hSd,hSc,hSf,hSs,U,hU,hUi,hUs,M,hM,T,hAll⟩
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure μ := hμ
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure J := hJ
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure ν := hν
  letI : IsMarkovKernel S := hS
  letI : Λ.IsCondKernel S := hSc
  have hPs (f g : Lp ℝ 2 J) : inner ℝ (P f) g = inner ℝ f (P g) :=
    inner_condExpL2_left_eq_right measurable_snd.comap_le
  have hTs : IsSelfAdjoint T := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.isSelfAdjoint_iff_isSymmetric.mpr
    intro u v
    change inner ℝ (T u) v = inner ℝ u (T v)
    rw [← M.inner_map_map (T u) v, ← M.inner_map_map u (T v)]
    rw [(hAll u).2.1, (hAll v).2.1]
    change inner ℝ (P (U (P (M u)))) (M v) =
      inner ℝ (M u) (P (U (P (M v))))
    rw [hPs, (hAll u).1, (hAll v).1]
    calc
      inner ℝ (U (M u)) (M v) = inner ℝ (M u) (U (M v)) :=
        hUs.isSymmetric (M u) (M v)
      _ = inner ℝ (M u) (P (U (M v))) := by
        rw [← hPs, (hAll u).1]
  have hcompS : ν ⊗ₘ S = Λ := by
    calc
      ν ⊗ₘ S = Λ.fst ⊗ₘ S := congrArg (fun ρ => ρ ⊗ₘ S) hSf.symm
      _ = Λ := Measure.disintegrate Λ S
  have hPreserve (u : Lp ℝ 2 ν) : (∫ y, T u y ∂ν)=∫ y, u y ∂ν := by
    have hi : Integrable (fun p : E × E => u p.2) (ν ⊗ₘ S) := by
      rw [hcompS]
      exact ((Lp.memLp u).comp_measurePreserving
        (show MeasurePreserving (Prod.snd : E × E → E) Λ ν from
          ⟨measurable_snd,hSs⟩)).integrable (by norm_num)
    rw [integral_congr_ae (hAll u).2.2.2.1, ← Measure.integral_compProd hi, hcompS]
    calc

        (integral_map (μ:=Λ) measurable_snd.aemeasurable
          (Lp.stronglyMeasurable u).aestronglyMeasurable).symm
      _ = ∫ y, u y ∂ν := by rw [hSs]
  let q : Lp ℝ 2 ν := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.L2Expectation.one ν
  have hq (u : Lp ℝ 2 ν) : inner ℝ q u = ∫ y, u y ∂ν :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.L2Expectation.inner_one_eq_integral ν u
  have hTq : T q=q := by
    apply ext_inner_right ℝ
    intro u
    calc
      inner ℝ (T q) u = inner ℝ q (T u) := hTs.isSymmetric q u
      _ = ∫ y, T u y ∂ν := hq _
      _ = ∫ y, u y ∂ν := hPreserve u
      _ = inner ℝ q u := (hq _).symm

  have hH0 (u : Lp ℝ 2 ν) : u ∈ H0 ↔ (∫ y, u y ∂ν)=0 := by
    change inner ℝ q u = 0 ↔ _
    rw [hq]
  have hInv (u : H0) : T u ∈ H0 :=
    (hH0 _).mpr ((hPreserve u).trans ((hH0 _).mp u.property))
  let T0 : H0 →L[ℝ] H0 := (T.comp H0.subtypeL).codRestrict H0 hInv
  have hT0 (u : H0) : (T0 u : Lp ℝ 2 ν)=T u := rfl
  have hT0s : IsSelfAdjoint T0 := by
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.isSelfAdjoint_iff_isSymmetric.mpr
    intro u v
    exact hTs.isSymmetric (u : Lp ℝ 2 ν) (v : Lp ℝ 2 ν)
  have hTn (u : Lp ℝ 2 ν) : ‖T u‖ ≤ ‖u‖ := (hAll u).2.2.1
  have hT0n (u : H0) : ‖T0 u‖ ≤ ‖u‖ := hTn u
  have hDef (u : Lp ℝ 2 ν) : inner ℝ (((1 : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν)-T*T) u) u = ‖u‖^2-‖T u‖^2 := by
    simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.sub_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.one_apply,
      ContinuousLinearMap.mul_apply, inner_sub_left]
    have hs : inner ℝ (T (T u)) u = inner ℝ (T u) (T u) := hTs.isSymmetric (T u) u
    rw [hs, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq]
  have hD : ((1 : Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν)-T*T).IsPositive := by
    apply (ContinuousLinearMap.isPositive_iff' _).mpr
    refine ⟨((IsSelfAdjoint.one (Lp ℝ 2 ν →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 ν)).sub (by simpa only [pow_two] using hTs.pow 2)),?_⟩
    intro u
    rw [hDef]
    exact sub_nonneg.mpr ((sq_le_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)).mpr (hTn u))
  have hDef0 (u : H0) : inner ℝ (((1 : H0 →L[ℝ] H0)-T0*T0) u) u = ‖u‖^2-‖T0 u‖^2 := by
    simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.sub_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.one_apply,
      ContinuousLinearMap.mul_apply, inner_sub_left]
    have hs : inner ℝ (T0 (T0 u)) u = inner ℝ (T0 u) (T0 u) := hT0s.isSymmetric (T0 u) u
    rw [hs, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq]
  have hD0 : ((1 : H0 →L[ℝ] H0)-T0*T0).IsPositive := by
    apply (ContinuousLinearMap.isPositive_iff' _).mpr
    refine ⟨(IsSelfAdjoint.one (H0 →L[ℝ] H0)).sub (by simpa only [pow_two] using hT0s.pow 2),?_⟩
    intro u
    rw [hDef0]
    exact sub_nonneg.mpr ((sq_le_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)).mpr (hT0n u))
  have hqa : (q : E → ℝ) =ᵐ[ν] (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) :=
    Lp.coeFn_const (α:=E) (μ:=ν) (p:=(2 : ℝ≥0∞)) (c:=(1 : ℝ))
  refine ⟨hμ,hJ,hν,S,hS,hSd,hSc,hSf,hSs,U,hU,hUi,hUs,M,hM,T,hTs,?_,
    q,hqa,hTq,hq,?_⟩
  · intro u
    exact ⟨(hAll u).1,(hAll u).2.1,hTn u,(hAll u).2.2.2.1,hPreserve u⟩
  · refine ⟨hH0,hD,?_,hDef,T0,hT0,hT0s,hT0n,hD0,?_,hDef0⟩
    · simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.sub_apply,ContinuousLinearMap.one_apply,
        ContinuousLinearMap.mul_apply,hTq,sub_self]
    · intro u
      rfl

end

lesson.statement: E is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert Borel space with canonical volume; rank zero is an explicit extension of the source Euclidean convention. V:E→ℝ is C²; 0<α≤β; α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖² for every x,v; η>0 and βη≤1. μ=volume.tilted(−V), J=Law(X,X+√ηZ) for independent X∼μ and Z∼N(0,I), and ν=J.snd. Finite dimensionality of E does not imply finite dimensionality of L²(ν). Let Λ be the law of (Y,2X−Y) under J, F(x,y)=(x,2x−y), and P the L²(J) conditional-expectation orthogonal projection onto the second-coordinate sigma algebra. The laws μ,J,ν are probabilities. There exist a Markov kernel S with, for every y, S(y)=volume.tilted(x↦−V((y+x)/2)−‖y−x‖²/(8η)), Λ disintegrated by S and both marginals equal to ν; an involutive selfadjoint linear isometry U with Ug=g∘F J-a.e.; an isometric pullback M with Mu=u∘snd J-a.e.; and a selfadjoint T on L²(ν) such that for every u, PMu=Mu, MTu=PUPMu, ‖Tu‖≤‖u‖, Tu(y)=∫u(x)S(y,dx) ν-a.e. and ∫Tu dν=∫u dν. There is a constant class q=1 ν-a.e. with Tq=q and ⟨q,u⟩=∫u dν for all u. Its exact closed orthogonal kernel H₀ is all of L²₀(ν). The full defect D=I−T² is positive, Dq=0 and ⟨Du,u⟩=‖u‖²−‖Tu‖² for all u. The actual restriction T₀:H₀→H₀ agrees with T on every u∈H₀, is selfadjoint and contractive. D₀=I_H₀−T₀² is positive, agrees with D as an ambient L² class on H₀, and satisfies ⟨D₀u,u⟩=‖u‖²−‖T₀u‖² for all u∈H₀.

steps.title: Recover the actual kernel and Hilbert operators
steps.text: Reuse the compiled actual Gaussian augmentation, reflected conditional kernel S, isometric reflection U, second-coordinate pullback M, and operator T. The kernel has the literal normalized density exp(−V((y+x)/2)−‖y−x‖²/(8η)); its stationary law and probability normalization are conclusions, not supplied premises.

steps.title: Transport selfadjointness
steps.text: The actual conditional expectation P is an orthogonal projection and U is selfadjoint. Move P across the inner product and use PM=M; the isometry M transfers the resulting symmetry to T.

steps.title: Prove mean preservation with the actual joint law
steps.text: The reflected joint law Λ disintegrates as ν⊗S and has second marginal ν. Each L² function is integrable because ν is a probability. The actual AE formula for T and Fubini therefore give mean preservation.

steps.title: Identify the constant and the entire centered space
steps.text: Take the canonical L² constant q=1. Its inner product is the mean. Selfadjointness and mean preservation imply Tq=q. The kernel of the continuous functional inner(q,·) is exactly all mean-zero classes, is closed, and is preserved by T.

steps.title: Restrict the actual operator
steps.text: Restrict T to the closed invariant subspace H₀. Its action as an ambient L² class is exactly T; symmetry and the norm bound transfer to this same restriction T₀.

steps.title: Compute both squared defects
steps.text: For either selfadjoint contraction, move one copy of T across the inner product. The result is nonnegative, so D=I−T² and D₀=I−T₀² are positive. Dq=0, and the centered defect is the actual restriction of D.

reconstruction.text:
For every finite-dimensional real inner-product normed vector space E with its Borel measurable structure and canonical volume (dimension zero is allowed), every V:E->R, every alpha,beta in the nonnegative reals, and every eta in R, assume alpha>0, alpha<=beta, V is C^2, eta>0, beta*eta<=1, and for all x,v in E, alpha*||v||^2 <= D^2 V(x)[v,v] <= beta*||v||^2. The Hessian is precisely the iterated Frechet derivative evaluated twice at v. There are no extra kernel, operator, invariance, spectral, or regularity inputs.

Set mu=vol_E.tilted(-V), namely normalized exponential tilting with weight exp(-V(x)). Let J be the pushforward of mu tensor gamma_E under (x,z)->(x,x+sqrt(eta) z), with gamma_E the standard Gaussian on E. Put nu=J.snd. Write H=L^2(nu;R) and K=L^2(J;R), spaces of almost-everywhere equivalence classes of measurable square-integrable real functions, with their real Hilbert norms and inner products. Finite dimension of E does not make H or K finite-dimensional.

For every E,V,alpha,beta,eta satisfying the stated assumptions, use the measures mu,J,nu and Hilbert spaces H,K defined above. Define Lambda to be the pushforward of J under (x,y)->(y,2x-y), and define F(x,y)=(x,2x-y). Let P:K->K be conditional expectation in L^2(J) onto the sigma algebra generated by the second coordinate, followed by inclusion into K; equivalently P is the orthogonal projection onto the closed subspace of second-coordinate-measurable L^2 classes.

Then mu,J,nu are probability measures. There exists a Markov kernel S:E->E such that, for every y in E, S(y,dx) is exactly the normalized exponential tilt of canonical volume with exponent -V((y+x)/2)-||y-x||^2/(8 eta). Thus S(y,dx)=[exp(-V((y+x)/2)-||y-x||^2/(8 eta))/Z_y] vol_E(dx), with Z_y the integral of this numerator. The formula holds for every state y, not merely almost everywhere. Lambda has S as a conditional kernel of its second coordinate given its first, so its disintegration is nu(dy) S(y,dx). Both marginals of Lambda equal nu.

There exists a real linear isometry U:K->K such that Ug=g composed with F, J-almost everywhere, for every g in K. U is involutive, meaning U(Ug)=g for every g, and its bounded continuous linear map is selfadjoint. There exists a real linear isometry M:H->K such that Mu(x,y)=u(y), J-almost everywhere, for every u in H. These maps and their properties are produced witnesses. In particular, M is an isometric embedding into K; the statement does not claim M maps onto all of K.

There exists a bounded continuous real linear operator T:H->H, selfadjoint, for which every u in H satisfies P(Mu)=Mu, M(Tu)=(P composed with U composed with P)(Mu), ||Tu||<=||u||, and Tu(y)=integral u(x) S(y,dx) for nu-almost every y. In addition, integral Tu dnu=integral u dnu for every u in H.

There exists q in H whose representative equals 1 nu-almost everywhere, with Tq=q. For every u in H, <q,u>=integral u dnu, and u belongs to ker(u-><q,u>) if and only if integral u dnu=0. This kernel H0 is the entire closed real subspace of H orthogonal to q, equivalently the entire mean-zero subspace, with the inherited Hilbert structure; it is not an arbitrary selected subspace.

On the entire space H define A=I_H-T composed with T. A is positive (its selfadjoint quadratic form is nonnegative), Aq=0, and <Au,u>=||u||^2-||Tu||^2 for every u in H. There exists a bounded continuous real linear endomorphism T0:H0->H0 whose value, included into H, equals Tu for every u in H0. T0 is selfadjoint and ||T0u||<=||u|| for every u in H0. With A0=I_H0-T0 composed with T0, A0 is positive, its value included into H equals Au for every u in H0, and <A0u,u>=||u||^2-||T0u||^2 for every u in H0. Thus both centered operators are actual restrictions of the corresponding full operators. All identities and positivity claims use the identity of their displayed full domain. No invertibility or quantitative strict contraction is asserted here.
